headline: Portable toilets for Shreveport and Bossier.
intro: From a crawfish boil in the backyard to a frac crew down in DeSoto Parish — porta potties, restroom trailers and portable sinks, delivered and kept clean.
sectionHeadline: Every rental is really a question about people and heat.
about: Here in Northwest Louisiana the summer does more to a portable toilet than anything else. A unit that holds up fine for a spring weekend needs more attention in August. So when you call ArkLaTex Portable Toilets, expect a couple of questions back — how many folks, how long, and how hot it is likely to be — before anybody quotes you a number.

faqs.q: How many toilets for a crawfish boil?
faqs.a: Figure on one for every 40 or 50 people for an afternoon, and more if it runs into the evening — boils go long and the drinks keep coming. Put a hand-wash station next to them; peeling crawfish is messy.

faqs.q: Does summer heat really make a difference?
faqs.a: It does. Heat makes a busy unit unpleasant faster, so in July and August a job site or a long event may need an extra service visit or an extra unit. We would rather mention it up front than hear about it later.

faqs.q: Can you get a unit down a gravel or dirt road?
faqs.a: Usually, yes. Tell us what the road is like after a rain. A truck that can get in on a dry day may not on a wet one, and the unit should sit where it can be reached either way.

faqs.q: Do I need a permit in Shreveport or Bossier?
faqs.a: On your own property, generally no. If a unit has to sit on a street, a sidewalk or city property, or it is for a public event, check with the city or the event organizer first.

faqs.q: How long can I keep a unit?
faqs.a: A day, a weekend, a month or the whole length of a job. Longer rentals are serviced on a regular weekly schedule.

faqs.q: Who do I call if something is wrong with a unit?
faqs.a: Call the same number on this page. Tell us the address and what is going on, and a service visit gets scheduled.

pages.intro: Home builders, remodelers, roofers, road crews and commercial contractors — a clean toilet on site keeps the crew there instead of driving to a gas station.
pages.seoTitle: Job Site Portable Toilet Rental Shreveport LA | ArkLaTex
pages.seoDescription: Construction porta potty rental for contractors in Shreveport, Bossier City, Benton and Haughton. Weekly cleaning and units sized to your crew.

sections.kicker: The cost of not having one
sections.heading: A crew that leaves to find a bathroom is a crew that is not working.
sections.body: Every trip off site to a convenience store is twenty people-minutes gone. That alone usually pays for a unit. And the federal rule says you need one anyway: OSHA's construction standard calls for at least one toilet for a crew of up to 20, then a seat and a urinal for every 40 workers until you pass 200, and one of each per 50 after that.

sections.heading: Plan service around August, not April.
sections.body: A unit shared by a big framing crew in a Louisiana summer needs more than the once-a-week visit that works fine in spring. If your crew is large or the job runs through the hot months, ask about a second unit or a twice-a-week service — either one beats a unit nobody wants to open.

sections.heading: Keep it out of the low spot.
sections.body: Red River country clay holds water. Set the unit on the high side of the lot, out of where runoff collects, and close to a firm drive so the service truck is not leaving ruts across your job every week.

faqs.q: Can it stay until we get a certificate of occupancy?
faqs.a: Yes. Construction rentals run as long as the job does. Call when you are done and it is picked up.

faqs.q: Do you put a sink in the unit?
faqs.a: Some units have a sink inside, or a separate hand-wash station can sit next to it. Either works well if the crew is pouring concrete or eating on site.

pages.service: Party and event portable toilet rental

sections.heading: Keep the guests out of your bathroom.
sections.body: One indoor bathroom will not hold up to a backyard of people, and a septic system out in the parish may not either. A couple of units by the yard keeps the line — and the mess — outside.

sections.heading: People, hours, and what is in the cooler.
sections.body: Start with about one unit per 50 guests for a party of a few hours. Longer gatherings and anything with beer need more, roughly one per 35 or 40. A 120-person reunion running from lunch to dark is three or four units with a hand-wash station beside them.

sections.heading: Downwind, on level ground, away from the food.
sections.body: Set them where folks can find them without walking across the whole property, but well away from the cooking. Shade helps a lot in summer. If the party goes past dark, make sure there is a light on the path.

faqs.q: Can you deliver on a Saturday morning?
faqs.a: Usually delivery is the day before or the morning of. Tell us your date when you call and we will work it out.

faqs.q: What about a festival with vendors?
faqs.a: Festivals need units spread out by crowd, plus hand-wash stations near the food. Send the expected crowd and a site map, and the layout can be planned from there.

pages.heading: Restroom trailer rental in Shreveport.
pages.intro: Flushing toilets, running water, mirrors and air conditioning — the next best thing to indoor restrooms at a wedding, a gala or a corporate event.
pages.seoTitle: Restroom Trailer Rental Shreveport & Bossier | ArkLaTex
pages.seoDescription: Restroom trailer rental for weddings, galas and corporate events in Shreveport, Bossier City and Northwest Louisiana. Air conditioned with flushing toilets.

sections.heading: In a Louisiana summer, that is the whole point.
sections.body: Guests in their good clothes do not want to step into a hot plastic box at an outdoor reception in June. A trailer gives them a cool, lit room with a sink and a mirror. For weddings, galas, debutante parties and corporate events, it is the one rental people actually remember.

sections.heading: Check the drive, the ground and the power.
sections.body: A trailer comes in behind a truck, so look at the gate width, low branches and how soft the yard is. It needs a flat spot and a power outlet or generator nearby. Most trailers carry their own water, so a hose hookup is nice but not required.

sections.heading: Pair a trailer with a few standard units.
sections.body: For large events, put the trailer close to the main tent and a few standard units off to the side for overflow. Guests use the trailer, and the line never backs up.

faqs.q: Is there someone there during the event?
faqs.a: An attendant can be arranged for some events. Ask when you book — it helps most at long receptions.

faqs.q: How early do I need to book?
faqs.a: Trailers are limited, so as soon as your date is set. Spring and fall weekends go first.

pages.heading: Wheelchair-accessible portable toilets in Shreveport.
pages.intro: Ground-level units with a wide door, grab bars and room inside to turn a chair — for festivals, parks, schools and family events.
pages.seoTitle: Wheelchair Accessible Porta Potty Rental Shreveport LA
pages.seoDescription: ADA and wheelchair-accessible portable toilet rental for festivals, parks, schools and family events in Shreveport, Bossier City and the ArkLaTex.

sections.heading: Any public event, and a lot of private ones.
sections.body: If units are grouped together at a public event or site, the 2010 ADA Standards say at least five percent must be accessible — and at least one, even if you only have a handful. For a family reunion or a church picnic it is not a legal question, but if Grandpa uses a walker or a guest uses a chair, it matters just as much.

sections.heading: No step, more room, something to hold onto.
sections.body: The floor sits at ground level, the door is wider, there are grab bars by the seat and enough space inside to turn around. Anyone can use one, so it can be your only unit at a small gathering.

sections.heading: A smooth way to get to it.
sections.body: Put it on firm, level ground with a clear path — not across gravel, a ditch or soggy grass after a rain — and keep the area in front of the door open.

faqs.q: Are they bigger than regular units?
faqs.a: Yes, noticeably. Make sure the spot you pick has room for the larger footprint.

pages.seoTitle: Portable Sink & Hand Wash Station Rental Shreveport LA

sections.heading: Crawfish, cattle and concrete.
sections.body: Crawfish boils and fish fries, food vendors at festivals, livestock shows and 4-H events, and crews working with concrete or chemicals. Anywhere hands get dirty and the nearest faucet is a long walk away.

sections.heading: Ask about your permit first.
sections.body: If you are selling food at an event, the parish health unit and the event organizer decide what kind of hand washing your permit needs. Ask them before you order so you show up with the right setup.

sections.heading: Pump, wash, done.
sections.body: A foot or hand pump pushes fresh water from a tank; the used water drains to a separate tank underneath. No hose, no power. It is refilled and emptied when the units are serviced.

faqs.q: How many people can use one sink?
faqs.a: A double sink handles a good-sized party. Very busy events or food lines may need more than one, or a service visit partway through.

sections.heading: Tell us the lease and who to ask for.
sections.body: Send the lease name or a map pin, the gate combination if there is one, and who signs for the site — the company man, a site supervisor or the office. Lease road directions from the nearest parish road save a lot of wrong turns.

sections.heading: Pipeline work does not stay put.
sections.body: As a spread moves down the right-of-way, units can move with it. Let us know a day or so ahead of a move, and the units are picked up and reset on the next run.

sections.heading: Lease roads after a rain.
sections.body: A lease road that is fine dry can be a different story after a storm. Say what it is like in wet weather, so units go where the service truck can still get to them.

faqs.a: Long rentals on location are typically billed every four weeks. Call for a quote.

faqs.q: Can we get a sink too?
faqs.a: Yes. A hand-wash station on location is common, especially where crews are eating on site.

sections.heading: Have three things handy.
sections.body: Where the unit is going, about how many people will use it, and the days you need it. Anything else — a locked gate, a soft yard, a spot way back from the road — is good to mention but not required.

sections.heading: What a service visit covers.
sections.body: The tank gets pumped, the unit is cleaned and sanitized, and the paper and hand sanitizer are restocked. Long rentals get this every week; events running more than a day get it between days.

sections.heading: Pickup.
